nodes.title: Help a user orient inside one workspace
nodes.body: A Brunch session should make the selected workspace and spec legible before asking the user to commit new graph truth.

nodes.title: Orientation should be selected-spec-first
nodes.body: The selected spec is the right unit for re-entry because workspace-wide summaries hide the concrete next move.

nodes.title: A workspace may hold multiple specs
nodes.body: Each spec has its own graph and sessions under the same local workspace.

nodes.title: Selected spec
nodes.body: The product-facing target of the current session.

detail.definition: The one spec whose graph and sessions a current interaction targets.

nodes.title: Selection must stay scoped to the chosen spec
nodes.body: The orientation flow must not blend facts from sibling specs unless the user asks to switch or compare.

nodes.title: Display the selected spec identity on session entry
nodes.body: On cold start or resume, the session must surface the selected spec name before asking for the next move.

nodes.title: Summarize settled intent facts before proposing downstream work
nodes.body: The session should name the goal, core thesis, and relevant constraints before deriving design or oracle material.

nodes.title: Keep orientation entries separate from graph truth
nodes.body: Process choices made at session entry must guide the kick without becoming spec claims.

nodes.title: Offer a deterministic route into downstream derivation
nodes.body: When intent is accepted and downstream planes are empty, the user should be able to ask for design or oracle projection from the entry menu.

edges.rationale: Multiple specs create the orientation problem.
Cross-spec leakage is ruled out for the orientation goal.
The derivation route depends on keeping process choices out of graph truth.
